We see material where
others see what remains.

NeoNaar is building a biomaterials platform around agricultural residues, recovering useful fractions and developing them for industrial use.

Our work begins with one question:
What useful material is still present, and what can it do?

Materials have a sourcing problem.
Biomass has a value problem.

Industry depends on highly engineered materials to control structure, stability, flow, coatings and performance.

At the same time, agriculture produces large volumes of biological resources whose useful fractions often remain underused.

Biological
resourcesFunctional

NeoNaar connects those two opportunities by turning biological residues into new material starting points.

Use more of
what is already there.

NeoNaar is developing an agricultural-residue biorefinery model.

Instead of extracting one component and treating everything else as secondary, we separate useful fractions and develop each around the function it can provide.

Performance without ignoring
where materials come from.

Use residues better

Recover useful material before biological resources lose value.

Build alternatives

Develop renewable materials that can be evaluated in applications currently dependent on conventional material systems.

Recover more value

Use multiple fractions rather than building the economics around one extracted product.

Design for industry

A material only matters if it works inside the customer’s process, formulation or final product.

The material landscape
is changing.

Industries are under increasing pressure to reconsider persistent and petroleum-derived material systems.

That creates demand for renewable alternatives, but renewable alone is not enough. The replacement still has to deliver function.

NeoNaar is developing materials that can be evaluated where structure, suspension, flow, texture and formulation performance remain essential.
